competitiveTarget: Beat Compass/Redfin/SIR About on STRUCTURE, not scale. OPEN on the firm story (small boutique brokerage · all of Central Oregon · help clients buy and sell) plus an optional Bend office exterior / mission band. Then client reviews as the primary proof (Google score + featured quote — never press). Then dated local closings. Then Contact four-up Call|Text|Email|Schedule. Then office 115 NW Oregon Ave #2 + firm OREA. Then a compact inquiry that GET-submits to Contact. FAIL if the page opens on brokers' faces, three equal broker Cards, or a Meet-the-Team dump. Brokers belong on /team only. About is the brokerage, not Meet the Team. Skip coast-to-coast, Redfin fee, and Rocket copy. Never invent MOS, prices, or licenses.

beats.text: Firm story opens the page: one plain boutique Central Oregon buy-and-sell sentence. Not a staccato three-liner. Not a staff-directory fold.
Brokers are not on About. No broker Cards, roster dump, Meet-the-Team band, or AboutTeamTeaser. Brokers belong on /team only.
Firm reviews as words (V3Proof) plus dated local closings as a carousel of recorded sales. Never invent MOS.
Equal four-up reach: Call, Text, Email, Schedule. No Call-dominant lead.
Office 115 NW Oregon Ave #2 is on the page. Optional exterior hero of that office.
Firm OREA license is on the page. One-line inquiry GET-submits to /contact.
Navy and cream only. Redfin is the layout and interaction reference, not a second palette.
Catalog interactions are real: closings carousel (shadcn carousel + Card) and inquiry input. Avatar-import plus cream CSS is not a demo match.

tasteReview.beats: Redfin's brokerage/office page — we win on the live filtered sales-density map with a real-time listing ticker and neighborhood-count pills, which no Bend competitor brokerage page shows; we lose on the reach bar and inquiry module, which read less finished than Redfin's contact block.

defects.finding: The four-up reach control is a flat white bar with plain black text and thin dividers — no button chrome, no hover/pressed state, no icon, nothing that reads as tappable. It looks like a table header, not the catalog Button Group demo it's supposed to be.

On desktop there is a large dead cream gap between the office card on the left and the floating inquiry input on the right — the input and Send button sit isolated mid-page with no visual relationship to the office card beside them, reading as an unfinished layout rather than a deliberate composition.

Three consecutive sections (hero, proof, closings) all repeat the identical eyebrow (small-caps label) → Amboqia heading → content rows → text link shape with no variation in width, density, or media — the stacked-section tell, even though each section's content differs.

Copy promises reviews shown 'one at a time' but the shot shows a single static quote plus a plain 'Every review' text link — no visible arrow, dot, or scrubber control that would let a visitor actually cycle through reviews, so the interaction the copy describes isn't demonstrated.

defects.section: neighborhood pill list under the map
defects.finding: Sunriver 150 / Summit West 140 / Mountain View 115 etc. are raw counts with no plain-English meaning and no visual encoding (bar length, shading) tying them back to the density map right above — a KPI list sitting next to a much richer visualization it should be reinforcing.

tasteReview.verdict: This is a correct, on-brand About page with one genuinely strong section — the live filtered sales-density map with real-time activity feed — surrounded by sections that are structurally complete but visually inert: a reach bar with zero button affordance, a proof block that claims rotation it doesn't show, and a dead whitespace gap around the inquiry input. demoMatch holds on the closings carousel and inquiry input, but the Button Group reach control looks like unstyled text, not the catalog demo. Every competitive-brief beat (firm story opener, no brokers, reviews+closings, four-up reach, office+OREA, inquiry-to-contact, navy/cream, real carousel) is technically present, so competitiveBriefPass is true, but 'present' and 'well-made' aren't the same thing here.
